No, this function is specifically designed for validating dates in the format of YYYY-MM-DD. Sure, here are a few quick tips for working with Perl:

1. Use strict and warnings: Always start your Perl scripts with "use strict" and "use warnings". This helps flag any syntax errors or potential bugs in your code.

2. Use Perl modules: Perl has a rich collection of modules available on CPAN. Take advantage of them to save time and improve the functionality of your programs.

3. Use regular expressions: Perl is known for its powerful regular expression support. Learn how to use regular expressions effectively to manipulate and validate strings.

4. Write modular code: Break your code into small, reusable functions and organize them into logical modules. This makes your code easier to read, debug, and maintain.

5. Document your code: Add comments and documentation to your code to explain what it does and how to use it. Perl has a built-in documentation system called POD (Plain Old Documentation) that you can use to write documentation for your modules.
